# EMA as Native UI App

## Important framing
EMA should be thought of partly like what happened when systems such as superpowers or GSD stopped being merely prompt/process overlays and started becoming more native products with their own UI/app shape.

## Main point
EMA is not just:
- a prompt system
- a workflow convention
- a CLI harness
- a note/graph substrate

It likely wants a **native app/UI form** that embodies its core concept directly.

## Why this matters
If EMA remains only a collection of:
- markdown structures
- prompts
- CLI flows
- hidden agent conventions

then it will stay indirect and harder to inhabit.

A native app/UI can make its real conceptual primitives first-class and legible.

## What the native EMA UI should expose
Not generic tabs, but EMA-native things like:
- planes
- objects across planes
- drift / gaps / reconciliation
- chronicle / review / recall
- active executions and bindings
- code / host / agent realities as part of the same system

## Best analogy
superpowers / GSD becoming more native is useful inspiration, but EMA should go further:
- not just native UI around agent workflows
- native UI around the full EMA conceptual model

## Implication for the new folder
The deliverable should keep asking:
- what is the EMA-native UI expression of this concept?
- what becomes visible only once EMA has its own app shell?
- what should stop being implicit once EMA is first-class product, not scaffolding?
